correctness.rationale: The rank-one sampled update decomposes orthogonally into scalar data defect and zero-sum coordinate martingale. Conditional row and coordinate independence gives the exact product-and-sum identities with every quantifier accounted for. The positive step and divergent cumulative step hypotheses yield pathwise contraction of the data defect and convergence of bounded monotone coordinates to an exact solution. The initial coordinate quadratic variation gives a strictly positive limiting solution-error floor. The rational 2x2 values were replayed by exhaustive independent branching, with all-step conclusions resting on the analytical derivation.

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact time-dependent solution-nullspace variance law for two independent samples, not the pre-existing qualitative fact that coordinate methods can approach random exact solutions. The 2026 source Algorithm 1 and exact-data Theorem 3.1 make an unconditional minimum-norm assertion that the rank-one example separates from its residual convergence. Older full-text results concern expected iterate, residual or full-column-rank mean-square bounds and do not state the all-admissible-step exact variance formula. Residual historical-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: An older general martingale or randomized-coordinate result could admit the exact rank-one variance formula as an unlisted specialization; absence of an indexed matching title or parameter is not uniqueness proof.

The qualitative existence of random nonminimum-norm limits in noninjective coordinate descent is already anticipated in earlier literature; only the precise double-sampling moment identity and universal all-admissible-schedule positive floor are assessed as new.

value.rationale: In an exact-data inverse problem, the natural goal is the unique initial-guess minimum-norm solution, not arbitrary feasibility. The positive nullspace floor for every divergent positive deterministic step schedule, despite residual and expected-iterate convergence, quantifies a structural barrier to that selection. Its 2x2 distinct-row construction falls squarely inside a current convergence guarantee and identifies which mathematical inference is not justified. This is stronger than a normalization check or merely another stochastic algorithm counterexample; the full time-dependent moment law is reusable for variance diagnostics.
